sources.citation: Goyal et al. 2010, Achieving Optimal Growth through Product Feedback Inhibition in Metabolism
sources.reusable_finding: Product feedback can support homeostatic control, while simple feedback can produce large metabolite pools; ultrasensitivity can constrain those pools.

sources.citation: Link, Kochanowski & Sauer 2013, Systematic identification of allosteric protein-metabolite interactions that control enzyme activity in vivo
sources.reusable_finding: Rapid nutrient switches and allosteric interactions can control flux on short timescales; organism-specific interaction identities are not imported.

sources.citation: Buffing et al. 2018, Capacity for instantaneous catabolism of preferred and non-preferred carbon sources in E. coli and B. subtilis
sources.reusable_finding: E. coli can reverse carbon flux rapidly through allosteric regulation, whereas B. subtilis requires additional interactions and transcriptional deregulation; species-specific details are not imported.

sources.citation: Goyal & Wingreen 2007, Growth-Induced Instability in Metabolic Networks
sources.reusable_finding: Coupled product-feedback networks can become oscillatory through a Hopf-like instability, supporting an explicit stability gate without importing model constants.
